call_points.text: FY27 EBITDA guidance held at mid-to-high teens, with H2 itself guided to high-teens growth on a high base.
call_points.versus_prior: reiterated the mid-to-high teens FY27 EBITDA growth given in the Q1FY27 call

call_points.text: Q3 RevPAR guided to double-digit growth, helped by festive weekends and a Bloomberg convention at its hotel.
call_points.versus_prior: consistent with the double-digit FY27 RevPAR growth given in the Q1FY27 call

call_points.text: Five contracted owned projects need ₹1,432 Cr, with ₹150 Cr spent and ₹450 Cr to be spent by end-FY27.
ESOP expensed in payroll from this quarter plus new headcount; ex-ESOP and Coorg flow-through is about 60%.
Dubai JV is EBITDA-positive but interest and depreciation drag PAT; renovation starts early FY28 for about a year.
Portfolio at 25 properties and 5,257 keys: 15 operational, 10 in pipeline, roughly half owned and half managed.
International room revenue mix recovered from a 10% YoY decline in March to a 1% YoY increase by June.
Ranthambore has slipped a couple of quarters on fortress wall stabilisation; management says it can fast-track once done.
Q1FY27 revenue and EBITDA expected to grow double digits, with May and June called exceptionally good months.
Management fees were about ₹95 Cr in FY26 and expected to grow double digits as managed hotels ramp up.
International share of business fell from about 50% to around 40%, with domestic rising to about 60%.
Sales and marketing costs rose because Expedia and Agoda moved to gross-basis commissions and GHA revenue share increased.
Net debt reduced by 50% in FY26, with net debt/EBITDA at 1.6x and an AA credit rating.
MICE cancellations in March were given credit notes and deferred six to nine months; management expects a high percentage to return.

operating_notes.text: FY26 same-store RevPAR rose 14% and ADR 13%; Q4FY26 RevPAR grew 6% with ADR up 15% to ₹32,000.
Portfolio stands at over 5,200 luxury keys across 24 properties: 15 operational hotels and nine in the pipeline.
Non-resident covers are 54% of total cover mix at city hotels; F&B is about 40% of hotel revenue and grew 15% in FY26.
RevPAR index rose to 1.4x from 1.3x a year ago; city hotels grew RevPAR 14% and resorts 24% in Q1FY27.
Direct bookings were close to 64% of business and website bookings doubled to 16%, at about one-third the cost of OTA channels.
Renewable share of energy is around 67%, targeted at 75%; all owned hotels have Platinum green building certification.
RevPAR of ₹17,225 in Q2FY27 was up 30% YoY, led by a 30% rise in ADR to ₹25,046, on owned domestic hotels including Coorg.
Non-room revenue exceeded 50% of total revenue in H1FY27; HMA fees rose 76% YoY.
Pipeline of 1,038 keys across 10 properties; Jaisalmer and The Leela Luxury Residences, Mumbai are in pre-opening with operations planned in FY27.
Q2FY27 suite occupancy rose over 700 bps, with paid suite occupancy in the mid-40s across owned assets.
Direct brand-website contribution to H1FY27 room revenue rose to 15.1% from 10.5% last year.
F&B mix was about 56% outlets and 44% banquets (groups and MICE).

timeline.summary: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts Limited announces Q4 FY26 earnings conference call on April 28, 2026, at 5:00 PM IST via dial-in.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹484.42 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹26.41 Cr.
Leela Palaces reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,527.3 Cr and PAT of ₹403.0 Cr, backed by strong RevPAR outperformance.
Leela's Q4FY26 earnings call guided FY27 occupancy to early 70s and Q1FY27 revenue and EBITDA to double-digit growth, with Coorg's first-year revenue at ₹65-70 Cr.

Leela's Q1FY27 call (July 31, 2026) reported 28% operating revenue growth to ₹352 Cr, 41% EBITDA growth to ₹143 Cr and five-fold PAT growth to ₹48.8 Cr, and guided to double-digit RevPAR and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹411.87 Cr (+32.6% YoY), net profit ₹94.59 Cr (+26.6% YoY).
Leela Palaces, Hotels & Resorts reported Q2FY27 revenue up 33% YoY to ₹411.9 Cr, operating EBITDA up 36% to ₹187.7 Cr at a 46% margin, and RevPAR up 30% on a 30% ADR rise.

Leela's Q2FY27 call (October 14, 2026) kept FY27 EBITDA guidance at mid-to-high teens with high-teens H2 growth, guided Q3 to double-digit RevPAR growth, and put the contracted pipeline at over 5,200 keys by FY30 with ₹1,432 Cr of owned-project capex pending.
